newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends firm after posting new high.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends firm after posting new high.

text.p: IPE Brent crude closed firm on Monday after renewed fighting in northern Iraq, fears of heating oil shortages and technical buying took the prompt contract to its highest level since the Gulf War, brokers said.

Nov Brent left last Tuesday's post Gulf War high of $24.70 a barrel in its wake as news of a weekend fire at a U.S. refinery underscored the precarious supply/demand balance for heating oil in the approach to the northern hemisphere winter.
"It was a reminder that things can go wrong," said a broker.
The prompt contract closed up 82 cents at $24.80 a barrel after hitting a new peak of $24.92 in late afternoon trade.
The market had been edgy since the open on news of renewed fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq. The United States urged Iraq and Iran to keep out of the conflict.

News that a fire had reduced output at BP America's refinery in Toledo, Ohio helped push Brent through technical resistance at $24.45 and the previous high of $24.70, touching off stop-loss buy orders along the way.
"Fundamentally there has not been much change, so a bit of Kurdish infighting and a refinery fire and that's it, off we go," a broker said.
U.S. heating oil stocks are well below year-ago levels.
Earlier, IPE Nov gas oil settled $7.25 a tonne higher at $234.00 after coming under some light selling pressure near the close.
The Nov/Dec spread gained a modest 25 cents to end at +$7.00 a tonne.
